- Heavy long-context generation (50k token windows, multi-turn user sessions) about 12k queries/day in peak;

1) Recommended SKU mix (H100 / A100 / L4) to match latency and memory needs while keeping cost predictable.

3) Any implications for KV cache sizing and prefix caching we should plan for.

Anya —

Thanks for the workbook, this is the right level of detail. High level answer up front, then a few operational bullets we should align on.

High-level recommendation (short):
- Core capacity: favor H100s for steady-state long-context inference (large KV + memory headroom).
- Cost/perf mix: use a small A100 tier for mid-length sessions and batch workloads.
- L4: excellent for stateless, low-latency short queries (embeddings and rapid chat), but won't meet the 50k token memory requirements without sharding.

Hedging plan: canary fallback to A100-quantized variants for transient H100 shortages, and L4 for stateless embedding spikes. We'll include autoscale burst slots into the Dedicated reservation to cover tail traffic.

Operational bullets we need from you:
- Expected 95th latency target for user-visible gen responses (ms).
- Percent of queries that require full 50k KV residency vs those that can use prefix-only caching.
- Any regulatory/network constraints that affect private endpoints.

Putting Karthik and Dev on the thread to pull numbers and a sizing workbook with slot counts + fallback rules. I’ll draft an ops handoff doc once we agree.

Folks —

I pulled the traffic sheet and ran a quick capacity model. Notes below by SKU and a recommended hedging topology. I attached a trimmed KV profile export as well.

SKU notes:
- H100 (80GB HBM): Best fit for 50k token residency without sharding. Provides ~2.8x faster decoding on long-context models vs A100 in our baseline kernel set. Good for steady-state predictable latency.
- A100 (40GB): Workable if you shard KV across slots and accept increased decoding time and coordination overhead. Best used for batched throughput and can be 20–35% cheaper per-token in high throughput scenarios when quantized.
- L4 (32GB GPU-class Ampere-style inferentia equivalent): Great for embeddings/short context and for bursty stateless traffic. Not recommended for primary long-context serving unless you partition conversations and rehydrate state server-side.

Hedging topology (recommended):
1) Primary pool: H100 reserved slots sized for 65% of peak steady-state long-context QPS.
2) Secondary pool: A100 reserved + ephemeral A100 burst to cover another 25% of peak. Use quantized model variants for cost parity.
3) Stat pool: L4 fleet for embeddings and short-turns (config route by token length).
4) Autoscale policy: warm standby slots in the secondary pool and fast-failover routing with preserved user-affinity (sticky routing by convo id).

KV cache sizing:
- For 50k token windows, estimate ~40–48GB per slot for active KV (model dependent). We should allocate ~1.2x headroom in H100 slots for safety.
- Prefetch/prefix caching: 30% of queries can be served from prefix cache in memory; ensure Redis or in-host cache for cold-starts to avoid repeated decode.

Attachments: kv_cache_profile.csv (attached)

Action: Karthik/Sojin, please translate these into slot counts and cost delta estimates for client review. Marcus — can you sanity-check the latency multipliers on our production H100 kernel set?

—Dev

Anya —

We translated Dev's topology into a client-ready sizing sheet (attached in the Drive link). Summary numbers below for the committed Dedicated purchase (monthly steady-state + burst pool):

Recommended committed mix (monthly equivalent):
- 24 H100 slots (primary): sized for 65% steady-state long-context load — expected 95th P99 gen latency ~1.1–1.6s depending on model and token length.
- 10 A100 slots (secondary reserved) + burstable A100 autoscale (up to 20 ephemeral slots) — used for batched workloads and quantized fallbacks.
- 12 L4 slots (stat pool) — embeddings and short-turn chat, routed by token-length policy.

Cost/benefit notes:
- H100 upfront cost higher but reduces request amplification from sharding and simplifies KV residency.
- A100 quantized variants reduce per-token cost (~25–35%) but add orchestration and a small latency penalty.
- L4 reduces net spend on embed-heavy volume by ~40% vs H100 if routed correctly.

Fallthrough policy (ops):
- If H100 utilization > 85% for 15m, auto-shift read-only prefix traffic to L4 and promote A100 quantized nodes for full-context requests.
- Maintain user affinity via sticky routing so rehydration is minimized.

Next steps:
1) Anya — confirm your 95th latency SLO and peak traffic day; we used your workbook peak numbers but want the official SLO to finalize pricing.
2) Soojin — draft the dedicated resource (VPC/subnet/firewall) checklist and the runbook for the fallthrough behavior.
3) Contract review: we’ll attach this sizing to the committed terms doc and share a pricing delta for H100 vs A100 heavy mixes.

I’ll set up a 30-minute tech deep-dive Wed 5/24 to walk Sparrow infra through the hedging topology unless you prefer an earlier slot.

Thanks —
